title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator on mobile takes notes of in-person conversations with speaker attribution
summary: The roadmap facts, licensing and published admin route are supported. The availability table incorrectly reports no documented automation: Microsoft documents app-centric availability through PowerShell, and the Facilitator setup page explicitly offers app-centric management. The claim that mobile attribution attaches people's names also goes beyond the published description.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > agent > Edit availability controls availability to everyone, selected users or groups, or no one.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents.
To change who can use an agent, select one or more agents and choose Edit availability. You can make an agent available to everyone, to specific users or groups, or to no one.

claims.claim: Automation for controlling Facilitator availability is not yet documented.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket automation absence in controls[0] and its rendered table cell with the documented app-centric call: kind 'powershell', call 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <Facilitator-app-id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/update-m365teamsapp?view=teams-ps'. Add to the existing row note: 'The Facilitator setup page documents app-centric management; this command sets app-centric availability to Everyone. Microsoft does not state here whether this automation also covers the newer Built-in Teams agents route.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management and the cmdlet reference. The setup page explicitly permits app-centric management, and its linked management page documents this cmdlet; do not imply that the new built-in route's automation was separately confirmed.
